rules.text: The Act s 109 defines the ‘levels’ for imprisonment
rules.quote: The Act s 109 defines the ‘levels’ for imprisonment

rules.text: If a level and a term in years or months are inconsistent, the level prevails unless there is a contrary intention.
rules.quote: If there is any inconsistent description of imprisonment in years or months and a penalty ‘level’, then the ‘level’ prevails unless there is a contrary intention.

rules.text: Generally, except for life imprisonment, an offence punishable by imprisonment may also or alternatively be punished by a fine of up to 10 penalty units per month of the maximum term (see also fine.maximum, 12.2: where the maximum is expressed in years only).
rules.quote: Generally, in Victoria, except for life imprisonment, if an offence is punishable by imprisonment it may also or alternatively be punished by a maximum fine of 10 times the number of penalty units than the maximum number of months of imprisonment that might be imposed for the offence.

rules.text: For a Level 2 offence and a natural person, a fine may only be additional to, not an alternative to, imprisonment.
rules.quote: If the offence is a Level 2 offence, and the offender is a natural person, the fine may only be additional, and not an alternative to imprisonment.

rules.text: A body corporate found guilty of a Crimes Act 1958 (Vic) offence may be fined up to five times the maximum fine for a natural person.
rules.quote: If the offender is a body corporate, and is found guilty of an offence against the Crimes Act 1958 (Vic), a court may impose a fine up to five times the amount of the maximum fine that could be imposed on a natural person found guilty of the same offence committed at the same time.

rules.text: A statutory offence with no specified maximum is presumptively two years imprisonment.
rules.quote: Where a statutory offence is created but no maximum penalty is specified, then the maximum is presumptively two years imprisonment.

rules.text: A common law offence with no fixed maximum is "at large": no legal limit, but the sentence must not be inordinate.
rules.quote: When there is no maximum fixed for a common law offence, it is said to be ‘at large’ and there is no legal limit on the maximum penalty.

rules.text: For an offence at large, the court may be guided by the maximum for similar statutory offending.
rules.quote: If a court needed to sentence for such an offence then it may be guided by the maximum fixed for similar statutory offending, and any sentence may be imposed so long as it is not ‘inordinate’.

rules.text: The penalty stated at the end of a statutory section is the maximum, not a mandatory penalty, unless the language clearly says otherwise.
rules.quote: Unless the statutory language clearly states otherwise, the penalty stated at the end of a statutory section is the maximum penalty that may be imposed, not the mandatory penalty that must be imposed.

rules.text: The maximum fine is fixed by the penalty unit value applicable at the time of the offending.
rules.quote: the Court of Appeal has indicated the maximum fine is fixed based on the penalty unit value applicable at the time of the offending.
